page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge is an x86_64 general purpose instance built on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor featuring 56 dedicated virtual CPUs across 28 physical cores with hyperthreading. The system includes 224.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance is not equipped with discrete GPUs and includes no local instance storage, requiring attached network-based block volumes for operating filesystem demands. Network throughput is provisioned with a 10 Gbps baseline.

Performance profiles reflect the capabilities and limitations of the Broadwell-era Intel Xeon architecture. Single-threaded benchmarks reveal weak metrics, indicated by a Geekbench single-core score of 948.0, a stress-ng single-core score of 1107.38, and low single-threaded compression throughput. However, its 56 vCPUs provide consistent mid-tier scaling in parallel workloads, evidenced by a multi-core Geekbench score of 9467.0, a multi-core stress-ng result of 40954.08, and a PassMark CPU score of 35028.65. Memory bandwidth sustains 104.82 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 50.54 GB/sec for writes.

From a cost efficiency and resource utilization perspective, the instance trades single-thread execution latency for wide parallel resource density. It is suited for horizontally parallelized enterprise workloads that require substantial RAM and multithreaded capacity without needing specialized acceleration or modern instruction sets like AVX-512 VNNI or AMX. Common suitable deployments include large-scale web application serving, batch processing pipelines, continuous integration clusters, and distributed in-memory caching systems such as Redis.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.14xlarge is a general purpose instance delivering 56 dedicated vCPUs and 224.0 GB of memory on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:4 core-to-memory ratio, this x86_64 virtual machine includes no integrated GPU hardware and lacks local instance storage, operating with a 10 Gbps network bandwidth baseline. Empirical benchmark results show low single-thread performance alongside steady multi-core execution, producing a Geekbench multi-core score of 9467.0 and handling 38.16 million Redis SET operations per second. The server provides balanced memory and thread capacity for concurrent, scale-out enterprise workloads that do not depend on high single-core frequency or local NVMe storage arrays.
